akhfash:2-2.t: He said ﴿وَطُورِ سِينِينَ﴾: its singular is "السِّينِينَة".

akhfash:7-7.t: And He said ﴿فَمَا يُكَذِّبُكَ بَعْدُ﴾: He made ﴿ما﴾ refer to the human being. On this view "ما جاءني زيد" is permissible in the meaning of "الذي جاءني زيد" ("the one who came to me is Zayd").

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿وَالتِّينِ وَالزَّيْتُونِ﴾, that is, the two foods, or two mountains in al-Shām that grow the two foods,

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿وَطُورِ سِينِينَ﴾: the mountain on which Allah the Exalted spoke to Mūsā; and the meaning of «سينين» is blessed, or beautiful with fruit-bearing trees,

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿وَهَذَا الْبَلَدِ الْأَمِينِ﴾: Mecca, because of the security of people in it, in the Jāhiliyya and in Islam.

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسَانَ﴾: the species ﴿فِي أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ﴾: the proportioning of his form.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿ثُمَّ رَدَدْنَاهُ﴾, in some of its individuals, ﴿أَسْفَلَ سَافِلِينَ﴾: a metonymy (kināya) for decrepitude and weakness; so the believer's work decreases from what it was in the time of youth, yet he has his reward, by His words, Exalted is He:

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿إِلَّا﴾, that is, but ﴿الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ فَلَهُمْ أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ﴾: cut off. In the hadith: "When the believer reaches an old age that renders him incapable of work, what he used to do is recorded for him."

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿فَمَا يُكَذِّبُكَ﴾, O disbeliever, ﴿بَعْدُ﴾, that is, after what has been mentioned of the creation of man in the finest form and then his being returned to the most decrepit age, which indicates the power to resurrect, ﴿بِالدِّينِ﴾: in the recompense preceded by the Resurrection and the reckoning? That is, what makes you a denier of that, when there is nothing to make you so?

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿أَلَيْسَ اللَّهُ بِأَحْكَمِ الْحَاكِمِينَ﴾, that is, He is the most just of judges, and His judgement with recompense is part of that. In the hadith: "Whoever recites «والتين» to its end, let him say: 'Yes indeed, and I am among those who bear witness to that.'"

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿وَالتِّينِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb of swearing; ﴿وَالزَّيْتُونِ﴾: conjoined to التين.

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿وَطُورِ﴾: conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿سِينِينَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿وَهذَا﴾: a demonstrative conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿الْبَلَدِ﴾: badal (substitute) for the demonstrative; ﴿الْأَمِينِ﴾: naʿt (adjective) of البلد.

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿لَقَدْ﴾: the lām occurs in the answer to the oath and ﴿قد﴾ is a particle of verification (taḥqīq); ﴿خَلَقْنَا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿الْإِنْسانَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿فِي أَحْسَنِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿تَقْوِيمٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is the answer to the oath.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿ثُمَّ﴾: a conjunction; ﴿رَدَدْناهُ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its object; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَسْفَلَ سافِلِينَ﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial), muḍāf to سافلين.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of exception; ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: a relative noun in the position of an accusative as the excepted; ﴿آمَنُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿وَعَمِلُوا﴾: conjoined to آمنوا; ﴿الصَّالِحاتِ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿فَلَهُمْ﴾: the fāʾ is a resumptive particle and ﴿لهم﴾ is the fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿أَجْرٌ﴾: postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position; ﴿غَيْرُ﴾: naʿt (adjective), muḍāf to ﴿مَمْنُونٍ﴾.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿فَما﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ indicating an implied condition) and ﴿ما﴾ is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿يُكَذِّبُكَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its object, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is the apodosis of the implied condition and has no grammatical position; ﴿بَعْدُ﴾: an adverb of time, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma; ﴿بِالدِّينِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿أَلَيْسَ اللَّهُ﴾: the hamza is a particle of interrogation and affirmation (taqrīr), and an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, the Name of Majesty being its noun; ﴿بِأَحْكَمِ﴾: the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and أحكم is genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar (predicate) of laysa; ﴿الْحاكِمِينَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

dervis-irab:1-8.t:
* I'rab:
(وَالتِّينِ وَالزَّيْتُونِ وَطُورِ سِينِينَ): The wāw is a particle of oath and genitive; (التِّينِ) is genitive by the wāw of oath, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted verb of the oath. (الزَّيْتُونِ) is also conjoined, and (طُورِ سِينِينَ) is also conjoined; the discussion of it has already been given, and we say here that al-Ṭūr, which is the mountain, is annexed to (سِينِينَ), which is the blessed place, so it is an annexation of the thing described to the attribute. It is possible to give it the declension of the sound masculine plural, and it is possible for it to keep the yāʾ in all cases with the nūn taking the vowels of declension. (سِينِينَ) is diptote, as sīnāʾ is diptote, because it is made a name for the place or the land, so it is a foreign proper name; had it been made a name for the place or the dwelling it would have been fully declined, because you would have named a masculine with it. ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, ʿUbayd Allāh, al-Ḥasan and Ṭalḥa read sīnāʾ with kasra and lengthening, and ʿUmar also, and Zayd ibn ʿAlī, with fatḥa and lengthening; this was mentioned in Sūrat al-Muʾminūn. These are variant dialect forms of this Syriac name, in keeping with the habit of the Arabs in toying with foreign names. Allah the Exalted swore by the fig and the olive because they are wonderful among the kinds of fruit trees. In al-Kashshāf: "A tray of figs was presented to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he ate from it and said to his Companions: 'Eat. If I were to say that a fruit came down from Paradise, I would say this one, for the fruit of Paradise has no stones. So eat of it, for it cuts off haemorrhoids and benefits against gout.'" And Muʿādh ibn Jabal passed by an olive tree, took a twig from it and cleaned his teeth with it, and said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'What a good toothstick is the olive, from the blessed tree; it sweetens the mouth and removes plaque.'" Al-Jāḥiẓ said in Kitāb al-Ḥayawān: "The fig and the olive are Damascus and Palestine." The disagreement about this is great; if you want more, consult the longer works.
(وَهذَا الْبَلَدِ الْأَمِينِ): Conjoined to what precedes. (الْبَلَدِ) is a badal (substitute) for the demonstrative noun, and (الْأَمِينِ) is an adjective. What is meant by it is Mecca; it was called "secure" because whoever entered it was safe before Islam. Have you not heard His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّا جَعَلْنا حَرَماً آمِناً وَيُتَخَطَّفُ النَّاسُ مِنْ حَوْلِهِمْ﴾? As for in Islam, whoever incurs a ḥadd penalty and then takes refuge in the Sanctuary, the ḥadd is carried out on him if he is one of its people; and if he is not one of its people, he is not consulted or dealt with in sales, and he is pressed until he leaves the Sanctuary, and then the ḥadd is carried out on him.
(لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسانَ فِي أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ): The lām is the response to the oath, and (قَدْ) is a particle of affirmation. (خَلَقْنَا) is a verb and agent, (الْإِنْسانَ) is the direct object, and (فِي أَحْسَنِ) is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from (الْإِنْسانَ); (تَقْوِيمٍ) is the muḍāf ilayhi. The wording of al-Zamakhsharī in this connection is very charming and is of lofty composition, so we have quoted it: "﴿فِي أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ﴾: in the best proportioning of his form and shape and the evenness of his limbs. Then the end of his affair, when he did not give thanks for the favour of that beautiful, upright, well-formed creation, was that We returned him to the lowest of the low in creation and composition, meaning uglier than the ugly in form and more deformed in creation, and they are the people of the Fire; or to the lowest of the low among the people of the lower levels; or: then We returned him, after that proportioning and beautifying, to the lowest of the low, when We reversed him in his creation, so his back became bent after being straight, his hair became white after being black, his skin became shrivelled after being plump, his hearing and sight became dull after being sharp, and everything in him changed: his walk became shuffling, his voice faint, his strength weakness, and his vigour senility." It is remarkable that Abū Ḥayyān says: "Al-Zamakhsharī took the sayings of the predecessors and beautified them with his eloquence and selection of words"; and after citing his wording in full he says: "This has some padding."
(ثُمَّ رَدَدْناهُ أَسْفَلَ سافِلِينَ): (ثُمَّ) is a conjunction of order with delay. (رَدَدْناهُ) is a past verb, agent and direct object, and (أَسْفَلَ سافِلِينَ) is a ḥāl from the direct object. Others preferred that it be an adjective of an omitted place, i.e. "a place lowest of the low", so that it is an adverb of place. I do not know why it escaped the minds of the parsers that it is a second direct object of (رَدَدْناهُ), because radda governs two objects in the accusative. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿لَوْ يَرُدُّونَكُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ إِيمانِكُمْ كُفَّاراً حَسَداً﴾; there the kāf and mīm are the first object, (كُفَّاراً) the second object, and (حَسَداً) a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), especially as it fulfils the condition for governing two accusative objects, namely that it be in the sense of "to make return". He said:
فردّ شعورهنّ السود بيضا ... وردّ شعورهنّ البيض سودا
(So He turned their black hair white, and turned their white hair black.)
(إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ فَلَهُمْ أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ): (إِلَّا) is a particle of exception; (الَّذِينَ) is in the position of accusative as a connected exception if we take the first meaning given by al-Zamakhsharī, or as a disconnected exception if we take the second meaning, and in that case (إِلَّا) is in the sense of (لكن) (but); (الَّذِينَ) is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause (فَلَهُمْ أَجْرٌ). The clause (آمَنُوا) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of (الَّذِينَ); (عَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ) is conjoined to the ṣila and falls within its scope. The fāʾ is a linker, because of the meaning of condition in the relative noun. (لَهُمْ) is a fronted khabar, (أَجْرٌ) is a postponed mubtadaʾ, and (غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ) is an adjective of (أَجْرٌ), that is, not cut off.
(فَما يُكَذِّبُكَ بَعْدُ بِالدِّينِ أَلَيْسَ اللَّهُ بِأَحْكَمِ الْحاكِمِينَ): The fāʾ is the "eloquent" fāʾ, i.e. "if you know this, O man, then what makes you deny?" (ما) is an interrogative noun of denial, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, and the clause (يُكَذِّبُكَ) is the khabar. The secret of this shift (iltifāt) will come in the section on Rhetoric. (بَعْدُ) is an adverb indeclinable on ḍamma because it is cut off from annexation in wording but not in meaning, i.e. "after these lessons and admonitions and the appearance of these proofs indicating the obligation of faith". It is possible that the address is to the Prophet, in which case (ما) has the sense of (من), and the meaning is: "who then denies you, O Messenger, regarding what you have brought?" The hamza is for confirmatory interrogation. (لَيْسَ) is a defective past verb, (اللَّهُ) is its noun, the bāʾ is a redundant preposition, and (أَحْكَمِ الْحاكِمِينَ) is genitive in wording and accusative in position as the khabar of (لَيْسَ).

* Rhetoric:
In His saying: ﴿فَما يُكَذِّبُكَ بَعْدُ بِالدِّينِ﴾ there is an iltifāt (shift) from the third person to address, with respect to the earlier ﴿لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسانَ﴾. The secret in it is intensifying the denunciation of man by speaking to him directly in address, as if it were said to him: what thing compels you to be a liar after these proofs, by reason of denying the requital?

farraa:1-2.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلتِّينِ وَٱلزَّيْتُونِ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: It is this fig of yours and this olive of yours. It is also said: they are two mountains in Syria (al-Shām). And he said on another occasion: two mosques in Syria, one of them being the one on which Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, spoke to Moses ﷺ. Al-Farrāʾ said: I heard [143/a] a man from the people of Syria, who was a man of tafsīr, say: «التين» is the mountains between Ḥulwān and Hamadhān, and «الزيتون» is the mountains of Syria. ﴿وَطُورِ سِينِينَ﴾: a mountain.

farraa:3-3.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَهَـٰذَا ٱلْبَلَدِ ٱلأَمِينِ﴾.
Mecca. He means: الآمِن (the secure). The Arabs say «الأمين» for «الآمن». The poet said:
ألم تعْلى يا أسْم ويْحكِ أننى * حَلفتُ يميناً لا أخون أمينى؟
(Do you not know, O Asmāʾ — woe to you! — that I have sworn an oath not to betray the one who trusts me [lit. my secure one]?)
He means: آمنى (the one who is safe with me). [Translator's note: «تعْلى» is as printed; presumably «تعلمي».]

farraa:4-4.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فِيۤ أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ﴾.
He says: We bring the son of Adam to the best of his form, which is his upright proportion and the full maturity of his youth, which is the best he ever is; then after that We return him to the most decrepit age. Although it [Translator's note: i.e. «الإنسان»] is singular, what is meant by it is: We do this with many people. The Arabs say: أَنْفَق ماله على فلان (he spent his wealth on so-and-so), when he spent only part of it; and this is frequent in the Revelation. Among it is His word concerning Abū Bakr: ﴿الَّذِى يُؤْتِى مَالَهُ يَتَزَكَّى﴾; He did not mean all of his wealth; He meant only part of it.

farraa:5-5.t:
And it is said: ﴿ثُمَّ رَدَدْنَاهُ أَسْفَلَ سَافِلِينَ﴾.
To the Fire. Then He made an exception, saying: ﴿إِلاَّ الذين آمنوا﴾, an exception from «الإنسان», because the meaning of «الإنسان» is "the many". Similar to it is: ﴿إِنَّ الإِنْسَانَ لَفِى خُسْرٍ، إِلاَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [Translator's note: Ibn Masʿūd] it is "أسفل السافلين". Had it been أسفل سافل, it would have been correct, because the wording of «الإنسان» is singular; but «سافلين» was said in the plural because «الإنسان» has a plural meaning. You say: هذا أفضل قائم (this is the best one standing), but you do not say: هذا أفضل قائمين, because you are referring by implication to a single person. When a single individual is not what is aimed at, its noun may be referred back to in the singular and in the plural, as in His word: ﴿والَّذِى جاءَ بِالصِّدْقِ وصَدَّقَ بِهِ أُولَئكَ هُمُ الْمُتَّقُون﴾, and He said in ʿAin Sīn Qāf [Translator's note: Sūrat al-Shūrā]: ﴿وإِنْ تُصِبْهُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ فَإِنَّ الإِنْسَانَ كَفُورٌ﴾, so He referred «الإنسان» back to a plural, and referred «تصبهم» back to «الإنسان», for the reason I have told you.

farraa:7-7.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَمَا يُكَذِّبُكَ﴾ [143/b].
He says: what is it that makes you disbelieve that people will be requited for their deeds? As if He said: who then can call you a liar regarding reward and punishment, after what has become clear to him of Our creating man as We have described?

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: His saying «والزيتون»: conjoined to «التين»; the wāw is not that of the oath, otherwise each of the two nouns would need an answer.

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: «سينين»: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr) with fatḥa because it is a diptote, on account of being a proper name and foreign.

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: (لقد خلقنا الإنسان في أحسن تقويم) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam); the preposition «في أحسن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الإنسان».

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: «أسفل»: an adverb of place, accusative (manṣūb); it was originally an adjective of an omitted place, i.e.: a lower place; and the clause «رددناه» is conjoined to the answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam).

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: The clause «فلهم أجر» is conjoined to the clause «وعملوا»; «غير»: naʿt (adjective).

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The clause «فما يكذبك» is resumptive; «ما»: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); «بعد»: an adverb of time cut off from annexation, the original being: after the mention of man.

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: (أليس الله بأحكم الحاكمين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive, and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar (predicate) of ليس.

mekki-muskil:2-2.t: His saying (وطور سينين): this is a dialectal form of (سيناء), and it has already been mentioned.

mekki-muskil:3-3.t:
His saying (وهذا البلد): the noun in (هذا) is (ذا) according to the Basrans, while according to the Kufans the dhāl alone is the noun. It is an indeclinable (mabnī) vague noun (ism mubham). It was made indeclinable only because it does not specify a particular named thing but moves to everything pointed at, so it does not settle on any particular thing; thus it differs from the nouns, and by differing from the nouns it came to resemble the particles, since particles differ from nouns; so it was made indeclinable as particles are. Al-Farrāʾ said: it is not declined only because its end is an alif, and the alif does not take a vowel. This is a weak view, which would entail the indeclinability of (موسى), (عصا), (مثنى) and the like. This has already been mentioned more fully than this.
His saying (فما يكذبك بعد): (ما) is an interrogative, nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (يكذبك) is the khabar (predicate).

mekki-muskil:8-8.t: His saying (بأحكم الحاكمين): (أحكم) is declined, although it is an adjective on the pattern of the verb, only because it is annexed, so it departed from resemblance to verbs, since verbs are not annexed; so it is declined into the genitive.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿والتين﴾: the wāw is a particle of oath and genitive, and «التين» is genitive (majrūr) by the wāw of oath; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted, its implied form being: "I swear" (أقسم).
﴿والزيتون﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, and «الزيتون» is a noun conjoined to «التين», genitive; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿وطور﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, and «طور» is a noun conjoined to ﴿التين﴾, genitive (majrūr).
﴿سينين﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive by the fatḥa.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿وهذا﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, and the demonstrative is in the position of genitive, conjoined to ﴿التين﴾.
﴿البلد﴾: a badal (substitute) for the demonstrative, genitive (majrūr).
﴿الأمين﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿البلد﴾, genitive.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿لقد﴾: the lām occurs in the answer of an implied oath, and «قد» is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq).
﴿خلقنا﴾: a past verb, and the pronoun is the fāʿil (agent).
﴿الإنسان﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb).
﴿في﴾: a preposition.
﴿أحسن﴾: a noun in the genitive (majrūr); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿خلقنا﴾.
﴿تقويم﴾: muḍāf ilayhi; the oath clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿ثم﴾: a conjunction for sequence with delay.
﴿رددناه﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿أسفل﴾: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object, accusative (manṣūb); or an adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted place, i.e. "a place lowest of the low" (مكانًا أسفل سافلين), so it is an adverb of place; or a second object of ﴿رددناه﴾, because «ردّ» takes two objects in the accusative.
﴿سافلين﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), the sign of its genitive being the yāʾ, because it is a sound masculine plural.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of exception.
﴿الذين﴾: a relative noun in the position of accusative by connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil); or the exception is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), «إلا» meaning "but" (لكن), and ﴿الذين﴾ is mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar (predicate) being the clause ﴿فلهم أجر﴾.
﴿آمنوا﴾: a past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿آمنوا﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿الذين﴾.
﴿وعملوا﴾: the wāw is conjunctive and «عملوا» is a past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause ﴿عملوا﴾ is conjoined to the ṣila, falling within its scope.
﴿الصالحات﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative by the kasra.
﴿فلهم﴾: the fāʾ is linking (rābiṭa) because of the conditional sense in the relative noun, and «لهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar.
﴿أجر﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿غير﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿أجر﴾, nominative.
﴿ممنون﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr).

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿فما﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ of eloquence (al-faṣīḥa), and «ما» is an interrogative noun of disapproval (inkārī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿يكذبك﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "it" (هو), and the kāf is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿يكذبك﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ ﴿ما﴾.
﴿بعد﴾: an adverb indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma because it is cut off from annexation in wording but not in meaning, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يكذبك﴾.
﴿بالدين﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يكذبك﴾.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿أليس﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (taqrīrī), and «ليس» is a deficient past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa.
﴿الله﴾: the Name of Majesty, the noun (ism) of «ليس», nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the overt ḍamma.
﴿بأحكم﴾: the bāʾ is a connective (ṣila) preposition, and «أحكم» is a noun genitive in form, accusative in position as the khabar (predicate) of «ليس».
﴿الحاكمين﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); the clause ﴿أليس الله بأحكم الحاكمين﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: The lām was assimilated into the tāʾ and the zāy because of its closeness to them. It is not permissible to pronounce it distinctly (iẓhār) with the lām of definiteness, because of its frequency in speech, but it is permissible with other (lāms) — even though it has been said of this lām that, together with what it is attached to here, it is a proper name. Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb said: «al-Tīn» is the mosque of the Companions of the Cave, and al-Zaytūn is «the mosque of Īliyāʾ (Jerusalem)»; so its origin is definiteness, and then naming occurred. Likewise the view of those who said: al-Tīn is Damascus and al-Zaytūn is Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis); and the view of those who said: they are two mosques, one of them being that on which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, spoke to Mūsā ﷺ. As for Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind, he narrated from ʿIkrima and from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: al-Tīn is this fig of yours and al-Zaytūn is your olive. Abū Jaʿfar said: These views, when analysed, come back to one meaning, because the oath is only by the Lord of the worlds, Mighty and Majestic; so the implied form is: "by the Lord of the fig and the olive".

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: It has been said: it is Ṭūr Sīnāʾ, in (various) dialects; and other than this has been said, which we have mentioned.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t:
This is the eloquent dialect. The noun (proper) in it (هذا) is ذا according to the Basrans, and ها is for drawing attention (tanbīh); according to the Kufans, the noun is the dhāl. It is not declined (muʿrab) because it is a noun that is not firmly established (ghayr mutamakkin), shifting (in reference), so it resembles particles; because it is not fixed upon a named thing, it must not be declined. Some grammarians said: because there is an alif at its end, and the alif does not take a vowel. Al-Farrāʾ said: if it were given a vowel it would become a hamza. Al-Khalīl, may Allah have mercy on him, said: the alif is an airy letter, so it is impossible to give it a vowel, because it is in the rank of a vowel, and a vowel is not given a vowel.
Abū Jaʿfar said: «ذا» is an overt noun (ism ẓāhir); what indicates this is the kasra of the lām with it [Translator's note: i.e., لِذا, as with overt nouns, not لَه as with pronouns]. Some grammarians said, in answer to one who asked why pronouns were given vowels but the vague nouns (mubham, demonstratives) were not: pronouns are in the positions of declinable nouns and had a distinction, so they were given vowels. Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard Abū Bakr ibn Shuqayr report this, and it is a good, well-founded answer.
As for al-Farrāʾ, he mixed everything up, saying: whoever says هو زيد with the wāw quiescent says هذا زيد; whoever says هو زيد says هذا أي زيد [Translator's note: the text here is garbled; the vowelling distinguishing the dialectal forms of هو is not shown]; and whoever says هو زيد with doubled wāw says هذاه زيد. Abū Jaʿfar said: The confusion in this is evident, because your saying هو with quiescent wāw is an anomalous dialect, while your saying هذا is a dialect in which the Qur'an came; so how can one be set parallel to the other, unless they correspond from another direction according to his view? That is, in your saying هو, the noun in it according to him is the hāʾ, and the noun in هذا is the dhāl — and this is his view, without disagreement from him. And part of the confusion is that in your saying هذّاه, the hāʾ according to him is for showing the vowel, yet he kept it in connected speech.
Al-Farrāʾ claimed that the evidence that the noun in هذا is the dhāl is the saying of the Arabs in the dual هذان, where they dropped the alif. This is not binding, because the alif only fell in the dual because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; and it was not permissible to convert it, so that one would say هذيان or هذوان, because it is not known to be converted from yāʾ or from wāw so as to be converted back to one of them; so nothing remained but deletion.
الْبَلَدِ الْأَمِينِ is a naʿt (adjective), or if you wish a badal (substitute), or if you wish a ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). Al-Farrāʾ claimed that الأمين is in the sense of al-āmin (safe), and recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 575-
ألم تعلمي يا أسم ويحك أنّني ... حلفت يمينا لا أخون أميني
(Do you not know, O Asmāʾ — woe to you! — that I swore an oath not to betray the one who trusts me?)
Abū Jaʿfar said: Al-Farrāʾ was opposed in this, and it was said: أمين is in the sense of maʾmūn (made safe / trusted) in both the verse and the line of poetry.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: The scholars discussed its meaning. From Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: He created everything bent over except man. ʿIkrima said: فِي أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ is youth, strength and endurance. Mujāhid and al-Nakhaʿī said: فِي أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ means in the best form. This is the best of what has been said about it, because the implied form in Arabic is "in a fashioning, the best of fashioning", (أحسن) being put in place of the thing qualified, i.e., in the most balanced fashioning and form.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t:
There is disagreement about it too. From Ibn ʿAbbās: to the most decrepit age; and from ʿIkrima: to the Fire. Muḥammad ibn Jarīr (al-Ṭabarī) claimed that the correct view is "to the most decrepit age", i.e., to senility, and this applies to particular people. He argued for the correctness of this that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, only enumerated what they had witnessed of His power, namely man's passing from youth to senility, and He does not enumerate against them what they do not acknowledge, namely entering the Fire.
Others said: This is not binding, because the proofs of Allah are manifest, and the signs of His Prophet ﷺ have appeared, so everything he informed of must be on the level of what is seen with the eyes.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t:
Whoever said the meaning of "to the lowest of the low" is "to the Fire" made الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا in the position of the accusative as an exception from the hāʾ in رددناه, because it has a plural sense. And whoever said "to the lowest of the low" means "to the most decrepit age" made «الذين» an exception not of the kind of the first (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ). And it has been said: there is an omission in the speech of the thing excepted from.
The implied form is: then We returned him to senility and dotage, until he became unable to worship Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and perform His obligations, and nothing is written for him [Translator's note: the text reads «ولا يكتب له شيء لهم», apparently for "except those who believed …: for them is written the like of what they used to do"] — for them the like of what they used to do. Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: فَلَهُمْ أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ, he said: He says: undiminished.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t:
The grammarians discussed this word (بعد), its explanation, the difference in its vowel, its nunation and lack of nunation, with more than ten answers. Among that is that the grammarians agree that قبل and بعد, when they are "terminal" (ghāyatān, i.e., cut off from their muḍāf ilayhi), are in origin not to be declined. They gave several answers as to the reason for that. Among the soundest is that the way nouns are made definite is by alif-lām or by annexation to a definite noun; so since these two were made definite by other than the definiteness of nouns, their being indeclinable (mabnī) became necessary. ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said: because they are dependent on what comes after them. And it has been said: since they do not move through the various case forms and are not firmly established (lam yatamakkanā), indeclinability became necessary for them. These are three answers.
If it is said: why was a vowel necessary for them? The answer is that Sībawayh said: "As for the firmly established noun that is put in a position in the rank of the non-established, it is their saying: ابدأ بهذا أوّل, and يا حكم أقبل". The explanation of this is that since أول, قبل and بعد had to be undeclined in one position while being declined in others, it was disliked to leave them without a vowel, so they were given ḍamma.
If it is said: why were they not given fatḥa or kasra? There are five answers to this question. Among them: adverbs (ẓurūf) take the accusative and genitive when they are not affected, and do not take the nominative; so when they were affected they took ḍamma, because ḍamma is of the kind of the nominative, which does not enter them in their sound state. And it has been said: since they resembled the singular vocative, they were given its vowel. And it has been said: since they are a terminus (ghāya), they were given the ultimate (ghāya) of vowels. These are three answers concerning the ḍamma, from the Basrans; we know of no others from them. The other two answers are from the Kufans. Al-Farrāʾ said: since قبل and بعد comprise two meanings, they were given ḍamma. Abū Jaʿfar said: The explanation of this is that they comprise their own meaning and the meaning of what comes after them, so they were given the heaviest of vowels. And Hishām said: it was not permissible to give them fatḥa, for then they would be as though annexed to what comes after them; nor kasra, for then they would be like what is annexed to the speaker [Translator's note: the text reads «المخاطب», "the addressee"]; so nothing remained but ḍamma. Abū Jaʿfar said: These are nine answers.
Al-Farrāʾ permitted آتيك بعدٌ يا هذا ("I will come to you afterwards, O you") with ḍamma and nunation, and recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 576-
ونحن قتلنا الأزد أزد شنوءة ... فما شربوا بعد على لذّة خمرا
(We killed al-Azd, Azd Shanūʾa, and afterwards they never drank wine with pleasure.)
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is outside what the Qur'an, the speech of the Arabs and reason have brought. He has no proof in the line, if its author is even known, because without nunation it is permissible (metrically) according to the experts in prosody, just as they recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 577-
شاقتك أحداج سليمى بعاقل ... فعيناك للبين تجودان بالدّمع
(Sulaymā's camel-litters at ʿĀqil have stirred your longing, so your eyes pour tears at the parting.)
He also permitted رأيتك بعدًا يا هذا. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a parallel; that is, he may have intended the indefinite. And Hishām permitted رأيتك بعدَ يا هذا, making it accusative and implying the muḍāf ilayhi, as though he claimed it had been pronounced since it was intended. Al-Farrāʾ and al-Akhfash claimed that the meaning is: "so who will deny you, after (this), concerning the Judgement?" Abū Jaʿfar said: This is not to be relied upon; «ما» does not occur in the sense of «من» except anomalously. The meaning here is sound, i.e., "so what drives you, O denier — what thing drives you to denial, after the appearance of the proofs and evidences, of the Judgement, whose news was brought by the one with the most manifest proofs?"

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: I.e., in His management and His making, no corruption or inconsistency enters your religion — and others are not like that.

safi-cedvel:1-5.t:
* I'rab:
(والتين) is attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being أقسم ("I swear") (هذا) is a demonstrative in the position of genitive, conjoined to التين, (البلد) is a badal (substitute) for the demonstrative — or an ʿaṭf bayān for it — genitive (اللام) is the lām of oath (قد) is a particle of certainty (في أحسن) is attached to a ḥāl from الإنسان (ثم) is for conjunction (أسفل) is an accusative ḥāl from the third-person pronoun (in رددناه) [Note: or it is an accusative adverbial attached to (رددناه), with an omitted qualified noun, i.e. "a lower place".]..
Clause: « (أقسم) بالتين ... » has no grammatical position; it is an opening clause.
And the clause: «خلقنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the jawāb al-qasam.
And the clause: «رددناه ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause of the answer to the oath.

* Morphology:
(1) التين: a proper noun for a particular mountain in Syria, or the name of the well-known fruit, a generic noun (ism jins); its pattern is فعل, with kasra then sukūn.
(الزيتون): a proper noun for a particular mountain in Syria, or the name of the well-known fruit, a generic noun; its pattern is فعلون, with fatḥa then sukūn.
(2) سينين: a proper noun for a particular mountain in Egypt; it is said that its meaning is "the blessed"; its pattern is فعليل, with kasra on the fāʾ and sukūn on the ʿayn.
(4) تقويم: the regular maṣdar of the quadriliteral قوّم; its pattern is تفعيل; its meaning is setting right and straightness.

safi-cedvel:6-6.t:
* I'rab:
(إلّا) is for exception [Note: or in the sense of "but" (lākin).], (الذين) is a relative in the position of accusative, an excepted noun, (الفاء) is redundant (لهم) is attached to a fronted khabar for the mubtadaʾ (أجر) , (غير) is a naʿt of أجر, nominative.
Clause: «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
And the clause: «عملوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the ṣila clause.
And the clause: «لهم أجر ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).

safi-cedvel:7-7.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is resumptive (ما) is an interrogative noun of denial, in the position of nominative, a mubtadaʾ (بعد) is an adverbial indeclinable on ḍamma, in the position of accusative, attached to (يكذّبك) [Note: the adverbial was cut off from annexation in form but not in meaning, so it was made indeclinable on ḍamma; the original sentence is: "What makes you deny after the mention of the creation of man and his return..."], (بالدين) is attached to (يكذّبك).
Clause: «ما يكذّبك ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

* Rhetoric:
Shift of person (iltifāt): in His saying, the Exalted «فَما يُكَذِّبُكَ بَعْدُ بِالدِّينِ».
It is an address to man, in the manner of iltifāt from the third person to the second, to intensify the rebuke and silencing, i.e.: what makes you a denier on account of the recompense and your denial of it, after this evidence?

safi-cedvel:8-8.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) is for the interrogative of affirmation (أحكم) is genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar of ليس.
Clause: «أليس الله بأحكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

* Morphology:
(أحكم): the elative from the triliteral حكم, meaning "judged"; its pattern is أفعل.

* Benefits:
- Mention of prepositions that have nothing to attach to:
From our saying "a preposition must have something to attach to" is excepted the redundant preposition, such as the bāʾ and min in His saying, the Exalted (وَكَفى بِاللَّهِ شَهِيداً) (هَلْ مِنْ خالِقٍ غَيْرُ اللَّهِ), and that is because the meaning of attachment (taʿalluq) is a semantic connection, and the principle is that verbs fall short of reaching nouns, so they were assisted in that by prepositions. The redundant one enters the sentence only to strengthen and emphasize it, not to connect. And al-Ḥawfī's statement that the bāʾ in His saying, the Exalted (أَلَيْسَ اللَّهُ بِأَحْكَمِ الْحاكِمِينَ) is attached is a mistake. Yes, it is sound to say of the reinforcing lām that it is attached to the reinforced governing element, as in His saying, the Exalted (مُصَدِّقاً لِما مَعَهُمْ) and (فَعَّالٌ لِما يُرِيدُ) and (إِنْ كُنْتُمْ لِلرُّءْيا تَعْبُرُونَ), because the truth is that it is not purely redundant, given the weakness imagined in the governing element that put it in the position of an intransitive one, nor purely transitivizing, since dropping it is consistently valid; so it has a rank between the two ranks.

semin-durr:2-2.t: His saying: {وَطُورِ سِينِينَ}: الطُّور is a mountain, and سينين is the name of a place, so the mountain was annexed to the place where it is. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «It is like سِينون and يَبْرُوْن in the permissibility of inflecting with wāw and yāʾ, of keeping the yāʾ fixed and moving the nūn with the inflectional vowels.» Abū al-Baqāʾ said: «It is a dialectal form of سَيْناء.» End of quotation. The majority read it with kasra on the sīn, and Ibn Abī Isḥāq, ʿAmr ibn Maymūn and Abū Rajāʾ with fatḥa on it, which is the dialect of Bakr and Tamīm. ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd], al-Ḥasan and Ṭalḥa read «سِيْناءَ» with kasra and the prolongation (madd); and ʿUmar also, and Zayd ibn ʿAlī, with fatḥa and the prolongation. Both have been mentioned in [Sūrat] al-Muʾminūn. These are dialectal forms that differ in this Syriac name, in keeping with the Arabs' custom of playing with foreign names. Al-Akhfash said: «سينين is trees, the singular سِيْنِية.» This is very strange and not known from the exegetes.

semin-durr:3-3.t: His saying: {الأمين}: This is فَعيل for intensification, i.e. those in it and those who enter it are safe — humans, birds and animals. It may also be from أَمُنَ الرجلُ with ḍamma on the mīm, أمانةً, so he is أمين (trustworthy); and its trustworthiness is its guarding those who enter it, just as the trustworthy person guards what he is entrusted with. It may also be in the sense of a passive participle (mafʿūl), from أَمِنَه (he felt safe from it), because it is safe from calamities.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا}: This is what is sworn upon.
His saying: {في أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيم}: an adjective of an omitted [noun], i.e. "in a fashioning that is the best fashioning". Abū al-Baqāʾ said: «"في أحسنِ تقويم" is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) of "الإِنسان"; by التقويم he meant القَوام (upright form), because التقويم is an act, and that is an attribute of the Creator, not of the created. It is also possible that the implied form is: "in the best form of fashioning", the muḍāf having been omitted. It is also possible that "في" is redundant (zāʾida), i.e. "قَوَّمْناه أحسنَ تقويم" (We fashioned him with the best fashioning).» End of quotation. There is no need for these strained interpretations.

semin-durr:5-5.t: His saying: {أَسْفَلَ سَافِلِينَ}: Two views are possible on it. The first: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the object. The second: it is an adjective of an omitted place, i.e. "to a place lowest of the low". ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] read «السَّافِلين» with the definite article.

semin-durr:6-6.t: His saying: {إِلاَّ الذين آمَنُواْ}: There are two views on it. The first: it is a conjoined exception (muttaṣil), on the meaning: We returned him lower than [all] the low in creation and composition, i.e. uglier than His [other] creation and most deformed in form, and they are the people of the Fire; so the connection on this view is clear. The second: it is a disjoined exception (munqaṭiʿ), on the meaning: then after that fashioning and beautifying, We returned him lower than [all] the low in the best of form and shape, in that We reversed him in his constitution, so that his back became bent and his sight and hearing weakened; and the meaning is: but those of the decrepit who were righteous will have a lasting reward. Al-Zamakhsharī said this, [here] summarised.

semin-durr:7-7.t: His saying: {فَمَا يُكَذِّبُكَ}: «ما» is interrogative, in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is the verb after it. The one addressed is man, by way of a shift of address (iltifāt); it was also said: the one addressed is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. On the first [view] the meaning is: what makes you a liar because of the Judgement (الدِّين) and its denial after this proof? I.e. you lie when you deny the recompense, because everyone who denies the truth is a liar; so what thing compels you to be a liar because of the recompense? The bāʾ is like the one in His saying, the Exalted: {على الذين يَتَوَلَّوْنَهُ والذين هُم بِهِ مُشْرِكُونَ} [al-Naḥl: 100]. On the second [view] the meaning is: what then is it that gives you the lie in what you report of the recompense and the resurrection — which is الدِّين — after these lessons, reflection on which necessitates the truth of what you have said? Al-Farrāʾ and al-Akhfash said this.

ukberi-tibyan:2-2.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَطُورِ سِينِينَ (٢)).
The words of the Exalted (سِينِينَ): it is a dialectal form of «سَيْنَاءَ», and it has been discussed in al-Muʾminūn.

ukberi-tibyan:4-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسَانَ فِي أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ (٤)).
The words of the Exalted (فِي أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ): it is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الْإِنْسَانَ». By «التَّقْوِيم» is meant «الْقَوَام» (upright stature), because «التَّقْوِيم» is an act, and that is a description of the Creator, not of the created. It may also be that the implied form is: «فِي أَحْسَنِ قَوَامِ التَّقْوِيمِ» (in the best stature of shaping), with the muḍāf (first term of the construct) omitted. It may also be that «فِي» is redundant (zāʾida), i.e. «قَوَّمْنَاهُ أَحْسَنَ تَقْوِيمٍ» (We shaped him in the best shaping).

ukberi-tibyan:5-5.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ثُمَّ رَدَدْنَاهُ أَسْفَلَ سَافِلِينَ (٥)).
The words of the Exalted (أَسْفَلَ): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object; it may also be a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted «مَكَان» (place).

ukberi-tibyan:7-7.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَمَا يُكَذِّبُكَ بَعْدُ بِالدِّينِ (٧)).
The words of the Exalted (فَمَا يُكَذِّبُكَ): «مَا» is an interrogative in the sense of disapproval (inkār), i.e. what is it that drives you, O man, to deny the Resurrection?

ukberi-tibyan:8-8.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلَيْسَ اللَّهُ بِأَحْكَمِ الْحَاكِمِينَ (٨)).
The words of the Exalted (أَلَيْسَ اللَّهُ بِأَحْكَمِ الْحَاكِمِينَ): that is, He is the Most Wise of judges, glory be to Him. And Allah knows best.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Tīn
Meccan
﷽
His saying: ﴿والتِّينِ والزَّيْتُونِ﴾ ("by the fig and the olive"): it was said: ”اَلتِّينُ“ is Damascus and ”اَلزَّيْتُونُ“ is Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis). And it was said: ”اَلتِّينُ“ is a mountain on which Damascus stands, and ”اَلزَّيْتُونُ“ is a mountain on which Jerusalem stands. And it was said: ”والتِّينُ“ and ”اَلزَّيْتُونُ“ are two mountains. And it was said: ”اَلتِّينُ“ and ”اَلزَّيْتُونُ“ are this fig that we know and this olive that we know.

zajjaj:2-2.t: ﴿وَطُورِ سِينِينَ﴾ ("and by Mount Sīnīn"): a mountain. Some read: ”وَطُورِ سَيْناءَ“; and this statement — and Allah knows best — is more fitting, because of His saying: ﴿وَشَجَرَةً تَخْرُجُ مِن طُورِ سَيْناءَ تَنْبُتُ بِالدُّهْنِ﴾ [al-Muʾminūn: 20] ("and a tree issuing from Mount Sinai which produces oil").

zajjaj:3-3.t: ﴿وَهَذا البَلَدِ الأمِينِ﴾ ("and by this secure town"): He means Mecca.

zajjaj:4-4.t: ﴿لَقَدْ خَلَقْنا الإنْسانَ في أحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ﴾ ("We have certainly created the human being in the best stature"): that is, in the best form.

zajjaj:5-5.t:
﴿ثُمَّ رَدَدْناهُ أسْفَلَ سافِلِينَ﴾ ("then We returned him to the lowest of the low"): to the most decrepit age; and it was said: to misguidance, as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿إنَّ الإنْسانَ لَفي خُسْرٍ﴾ [al-ʿAṣr: 2] ﴿إلا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ﴾ [al-ʿAṣr: 3] ("the human being is surely in loss, except those who believe and do righteous deeds"). And it is — and Allah knows best — that the creation of creatures is upon the natural disposition (fiṭra), so whoever disbelieves and goes astray is the one returned to the lowest of the low.
﴿إلا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ﴾ [al-Tīn: 6]: that is, except these, for they are not returned to the lowest of the low.

zajjaj:6-6.t: And His saying: ﴿فَلَهم أجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ﴾: that is, it is not held up to them as a favour (lā yumannu ʿalayhim); and it was said: ”غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ“ means "uninterrupted". And the answer to the oath in His saying ﴿والتِّينِ والزَّيْتُونِ﴾ [al-Tīn: 1] is His saying: ﴿لَقَدْ خَلَقْنا الإنْسانَ في أحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ﴾ [al-Tīn: 4].
